title: Malaysian Used-Car Listings — Daily Snapshots
subtitle: Daily append-only snapshots of a Malaysian used-car index
description:
Daily snapshots of a Malaysian used-car listing index (motortrader.com.my), collected since 2026-07-19 and still running. Append-only: a price change is a new dated row, never an overwrite, so price cuts and listing removals are directly measurable.

Malaysian used-car *listing dynamics* -- how long ads stay up, how much sellers cut -- are not published anywhere. Asking prices are everywhere; what happens to a listing over time is not.

READ THIS FIRST -- what this dataset cannot do. It cannot tell you how long a car takes to sell, and no amount of extra collection will change that. A listing disappearing means expired, relisted, missed by the crawl, or sold, unlabelled. Refitting the exit rule on the full window found 60.2% of 5-day absences still come back and no absence threshold clears a 5% reversal bar on evidence. The column formerly called event_exited is renamed absent_ge_5_obs_days in this version to stop it being used as a survival event. Full argument: https://lotclock.netlify.app

What it does support: inventory levels, asking-price behaviour, price-cut timing and size, and how long an *ad* stays up -- each named as what it is.

Two files. Read lotclock_daily_coverage.csv first: it says which days were actually walked properly, because a listing being absent means nothing on a day the crawl was capped or killed mid-run. lotclock_listings.csv has one row per listing in the full-census era.

How to use it honestly:
- Do not pool the coverage eras. Before 2026-08-09 the crawl harvested only ~15% of the site, which oversampled long-lived listings.
- Duration is in observed days, not calendar days. Collection has gaps.
- absent_ge_5_obs_days is an absence, not an exit and not a sale. Do not fit a survival model on it.
- The sample is one dealer-heavy index skewing premium and Klang Valley (median asking price around RM 181,000; KL plus Selangor are ~98% of rows). It is not the Malaysian market.
- make/model come from a naive title split, so "LAND ROVER" parses as make LAND, model ROVER. Apply a marque list if you need clean makes.

Collected honouring robots.txt and the published crawl-delay. No proxy rotation, no IP rotation, no evasion, no login-walled content. Public index only. No personal data of any seller is collected or published, and raw HTML is not redistributed -- derived tables only.

Full method and caveats in DATA_CARD.md. Source code: https://github.com/talvin29/LotClock

resources.description: One row per collection day. Read this first — it declares which days were actually walked properly. A listing being absent only means something on a day the site was fully crawled; days flagged 0 are page-capped or killed mid-walk, and treating them as light days invents mass disappearances.

fields.name: listings_seen
fields.description: Number of listing rows harvested that day.

fields.name: coverage_era
fields.description: partial_15pct before 2026-08-09 (crawl capped at ~15% of the site), full_census from then on. Do not pool the two eras.

fields.name: is_observation_day
fields.description: 1 only if this is a full-census day that completed (>=10,000 rows). Absence of a listing is only informative on these days.

resources.description: One row per listing observed on a full-census observation day: asking prices, price cuts, observed days seen, and an absence flag. NOT a survival table -- the exit event is not in this data, see the dataset description and DATA_CARD.md.

fields.name: listing_id
fields.description: Stable listing id from the source index.

fields.name: make
fields.description: First token after the year in the listing title. Naive split: LAND ROVER parses as make LAND. Apply a marque list if you need clean makes.

fields.name: model
fields.description: Second token after the year in the listing title. Same naive-split caveat as make.

fields.name: mileage_band
fields.description: Mileage band as displayed on the listing, not an odometer reading.

fields.name: location_state
fields.description: Malaysian state as listed. KL plus Selangor are roughly 98% of rows.

fields.name: first_price_myr
fields.description: First asking price observed for this listing, in MYR. 57 listings have no parsed price.

fields.name: last_price_myr
fields.description: Most recent asking price observed for this listing, in MYR.

fields.name: price_cut_myr
fields.description: first_price_myr minus last_price_myr. 0 if the asking price was never cut. This is an asking-price cut, not a negotiated discount.

fields.name: observed_days_seen
fields.description: Number of observation days on which this listing appeared.

fields.name: duration_obs_days
fields.description: First-to-last sighting, inclusive, counted in observed days rather than calendar days. Collection has gaps.

fields.name: absent_ge_5_obs_days
fields.description: 1 if the listing was not seen for 5 consecutive observation days. This is an ABSENCE, not an event and not a sale. Renamed from event_exited on 2026-08-25: refitting the exit rule on the full window showed 60.2% of 5-day absences still come back, and no threshold clears a 5% reversal bar on the available evidence. Do not use this as a survival event.

fields.name: listed_before_census
fields.description: 1 if the listing was already present in the partial-coverage era, meaning its true time on market started before observation began (left-truncated).
